t: A tiny low-cost RISC-V chip with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth for small smart gadgets.
steps: Buy a Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32C3 from Seeed Studio for about 5 US dollars, or a QT Py ESP32-C3 from Adafruit for about 10.
Plug the board into your computer with a USB-C cable that carries data.
Install the free Arduino IDE and add the ESP32 board package.
Pick your board and turn on USB CDC On Boot in the Tools menu.
Upload the WiFiScan example and open the Serial Monitor to list the networks around you.
Hold the Boot button while plugging in the board to recover a stuck upload.
Try MicroPython with Thonny or flash WLED from its web installer later.
meta: Open Board. From $4.90. Easy to find.
